text:
Drake Batherson scored three times, and the third came with 12 seconds left, a deflection that made it OTT 7, NYR 4 and capped a night that was louder than it was close. Batherson, drafted 121st overall in 2017 out of the Cape Breton Eagles, had two of his goals in the first 12 minutes of the game, then finished it off. Ottawa was up 4-1 in the second period and again 6-4 late, and answered every Rangers push.

The surprise is how the game was played. Our numbers say the Rangers deserved to win, and by a wide margin. "Deserved to win" is the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, and NYR took 64 percent of them. They had 67 shot attempts to 52 and out-chanced Ottawa in expected goals (the quality of the looks) at even strength, 2.77 to 2.39. They owned the third period, 1.55 to 0.63 in expected goals, and Alexis Lafrenière's best look, a 29 percent chance in the first, was stopped.

Part of the gap was in net. Dylan Garand allowed about two goals more than his shots deserved, while Jonas Johansson broke roughly even. Ottawa also hit harder, 34 hits to 21, and blocked 19 shots to 13, and it took the chances that counted. We'd watch whether the Rangers keep generating this volume with a steadier night in goal; the facts we have don't give either team's record or streak.
